And they {{ls}}aid, concerning {{sc|Iesvs}} of Nazareth, vvho vvas a man a Prophet, mightie in vvorke and vvorde before God and al the people. {{verse|chapter=24|verse=20}} And hovv our cheefe Prie{{ls}}tes and Princes deliuered him into condemnation of death, and crucified him. {{verse|chapter=24|verse=21}} but vve hoped that it vvas he that {{ls}}hould redeeme I{{ls}}rael: and novv be{{ls}}ides al this, to day is the third day {{ls}}ince the{{ls}}e things vvere done. {{verse|chapter=24|verse=22}} But certaine vvomen al{{ls}}o of ours, made vs afraid: vvho before it vvas light, vvere at the monument, {{verse|chapter=24|verse=23}} and not finding his body, came, {{ls}}aying that they {{ls}}avv a vi{{ls}}ion al{{ls}}o of Angels, vvho {{ls}}ay that he is aliue. {{verse|chapter=24|verse=24}} And certaine men of ours vvent to the monument: and they found it {{ls}}o as the vvomen {{ls}}aid, but him they found not. {{verse|chapter=24|verse=25}} And he {{ls}}aid to them, O foli{{ls}}h, and {{ls}}lovv of hart to beleeue, in al things vvhich the Prophets haue {{ls}}poken. {{verse|chapter=24|verse=26}} Ought not Chri{{ls}}t to haue {{ls}}uffred the{{ls}}e things, and {{ls}}o to enter into his glorie? {{verse|chapter=24|verse=27}} And beginning from Moy{{ls}}es and al the Prophets, he did interpret to them in al the {{ls}}criptures the things that vvere concerning him. {{verse|chapter=24|verse=28}} And they drevv nigh to the tovvne vvhither they vvent: and he made {{ls}}emblaunce to goe further. {{verse|chapter=24|verse=29}} And they forced<noinclude>{{rh||Dd ij|him,}}</noinclude>
